english_classification.chapter_title: The Chapter of the Four Kingdoms
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter contains NO cosmological-correspondential substrate. Teaching purity is 0.000. The entire chapter is a Manichaean homiletic composition: Mani takes a Jesus saying (Matt 10:42) about giving a cup of water, lists four contemporary political kingdoms (Babylon/Persia, Rome, Axumites, Silis) as a rhetorical foil, and argues that alms-giving to disciples and catechumens surpasses worldly greatness. The 'four kingdoms' are earthly political entities, not cosmic domains — no degree mapping, no correspondential structure. Every paragraph either frames, cites scripture, applies to church categories, or exhorts. Gardner notes the unusual reference to the Holy Spirit rather than the Light Mind, confirming this is a distinctively Manichaean ecclesiastical composition rather than transmitted older teaching.
